key_insight: GitOfThoughts makes LLM reasoning version-controlled and replayable with git, but the paper finds memory usually does not improve accuracy unless the retrieved case is nearly a duplicate of the current problem.
engineering_relevance: The main value is auditability, provenance, and mergeable agent memory at near-zero integration cost, rather than a general accuracy boost.
method: Stores each scored thought as a git commit
Uses scores as notes, outcomes as tags, and retrieval via git log
Compares five memory substrates across two benchmarks, two model scales, and pre-registered replications
evidence_signal: Across none, markdown, vector, graph, and git memory, novel-problem accuracy did not improve reliably; gains appeared only when similarity exceeded roughly 0.8, and the early positive result failed replication.
watch_item: Git-based memory improves traceability, but it should not be assumed to transfer methods or raise accuracy beyond near-duplicate retrieval cases.
paper_title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge
